Confirmed.

This is actually a bug with cairo (try type="Xlib" or something else in argument type for a workaround), I guess some numerical rounding problem.

Minimal example to reproduce it:

png("ImageWithWhiteStripe.png", width = 330, height = 200, type = "cairo")
image(matrix(1, nrow = 300, ncol = 1))
dev.off()

comments.text:
This looks pretty good.  Thanks!  A couple of comments:

1.
The rounding in cairoRect() should only be needed for raster devices (which can be checked by looking at `xd->type` - see cairoBM.h and some examples in `switch` statements in cairoBM.c).

2.
Using round() (in C) might still result in some odd behaviour if the rounding mode is "round to even", like it is for round() in R ...

```
> round(seq(0, 2, .5))
[1] 0 0 1 2 2
```

For example, this variation on the simple bug would still draw no line because the .5 would round to 0 ...

```
png("bug-2-cairo.png", type="cairo", width=100, height=100)
grid.rect(x=0, width=.005, just="left", gp=gpar(col=NA, fill="red"))
dev.off()
```

That does NOT happen on my system (gcc Ubuntu 20.04), but maybe it is possible on other systems.  One way to ensure always rounding up (at least for the positive values we will be dealing with) is to add .5 and then truncate, for example, in R ...

```
> trunc(seq(0, 2, .5) + .5)
[1] 0 1 1 2 2
```

So the equivalent in C, perhaps `(int)(x + .5)`, might be an even safer option. Sort of half-way between Quartz and Xlib :)

3.
Yes, testing would be great.  At least the usual `make check-devel`, but also some visual regression testing (e.g., with {gdiff}) on the examples from 'graphics', 'grid', 'lattice', and 'ggplot2' would be handy.

comments.text:
Created attachment 3417
Proposed patch for Cairo

Hi Paul, hope you're well.

> The rounding in cairoRect() should only be needed for raster devices (which can be checked by looking at `xd->type` ...

Good catch. I assume the raster devices are `PNG`, `PNGdirect`, `JPEG`, `TIFF`, and `BMP`, and the other types may be left alone without the correction? Latest version of the proposed patch implementing that is attached.

> Using `round()` (in C) might still result in some odd behaviour if the rounding mode is "round to even"

I believe the C standard ensures that `round()` will never use "round to even", instead always rounding away from zero. I have no definitive reference, but quoting from [1]:

"Computes the nearest integer value to arg (in floating-point format), rounding halfway cases away from zero, regardless of the current rounding mode."


[1] https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/numeric/math/round

> At least the usual `make check-devel`, but also some visual regression testing (e.g., with {gdiff}) on the examples from 'graphics', 'grid', 'lattice', and 'ggplot2' would be handy.

The `check-devel` target seems to pass with no issues.

```
$ make check-devel
[... snip ...]
* DONE

Status: OK
```

I used {gdiff} to generate some reference files from both current devel and this patched R, using e.g. `gdiffPackage("graphics")` and `gdiffCompare(controlDir = [...])`

There does appear to be several differences, output summaries are attached. On visual inspection, (at least for me) the differences look to be minor to the eye. I've attached what appear to be the worst offenders for comparison.

comments.text:
Thanks for all of the testing work (and the latest patch).

Unfortunately, that is quite a large number of differences (particularly for {lattice} and {ggplot}).  I would expect to see some differences when there are rectangles being drawn because the patch may introduce 1-pixel changes in rectangle width or height.  However, the example differences that you attached, e.g., a difference in an arrow head, appear to have nothing to do with rectangles.

Were there any differences that involve drawing rectangles?  e.g., perhaps the lattice::barchart() ones?

The fact that the differences are not particularly visible to the naked eye does not save us.  That is one of the specific advantages of automated visual diff'ing like what {gdiff} provides.  Not only are we saved from the tedium of visual inspection, but we will pick up changes that our eyes might not spot.  If there is a difference between two PNGs that are both produced by Cairo, particularly on the same platform, and particularly not involving any text (fonts), there really should be a reason for that difference in the code.

Unfortunately, I cannot immediately think of what the source of those differences might be.  It may require debugging the example that produces the different images, on both unpatched and patched R, tracking it down to calls on the Cairo device, and seeing if anything, including anything in the 'gc' structure, is different.

Another thing to check for {lattice} and {ggplot2} is that you have exactly the same package version (and in the case of {ggplot2} then same package versions for all dependencies) on both patched and unpatched R.

Thanks for the review. You are correct, there was indeed something else going on affecting the plots... drat!

I'm not sure what the issue was (perhaps a consequence of running unpatched R in RStudio; or perhaps I messed up setting the `device = ` argument), but I've rebuilt both patched and unpatched R from scratch, gave them a freshly installed library, and ran the R processes directly in a terminal. With that, the set of changes from {gdiff} is smaller, though still quite a lot for {ggplot2}. I've updated the `differ_log.txt` attachment.

I've also grabbed the files that now differ and updated the `gdiff-offenders.zip` attachment. The differences do now look to be related to drawing rectangles, with what seems to be shifts of a single pixel when drawing axes and/or data. I have to leave this for now, but if further investigation is required a future explorer could take a closer look at specific examples at a future R dev day.

The patch is unchanged from the previous version, I just redid my testing analysis (more carefully, it seems...)

Apologies for the previous noise and thanks for the {gdiff} tips!

George

comments.text: Hi George and Paul. Thanks for your continued work and comments on this. I'm happy to pick it up again for future exploration (though won't get a chance to look at this again until towards the end of November).

Thanks for the update George.  That is starting to make a lot more sense.  As you say, the differences now at least appear to be related to drawing rectangles (that are filled with no border), which is where we would expect differences to occur.  There are also a LOT of replications of or minor variations on the same plot in the ggplot2 set, so the 39 differences are in reality fewer than that.  Furthermore, the differences all appear to be single-pixel-width and not visible to the naked eye, so not likely to have a visual impact.

In fact, if you zoom in, say to 700%, on, for example, *-scale_colour_viridis_c-007.png, you can see the extra pixel width that is added in the patch version on the left-most bar, and you can also see that some bars are a pixel wider than others, where in theory they should all be the same width.  So this looks like exactly the sort of change that we would expect to see occurring.

The *-panel.smoothScatter-003.png case is interesting.  The dots are drawn with pch='.', which the graphics engine attempts to draw as a single pixel (see GESymbol in engine.c), so we are right in the zone for this issue.  If you zoom in on the current vs patched versions, and switch between, you can see a couple of individual dots jumping one pixel up/down or left/right.

One issue with committing this change is that it could trigger any visual-diff code that other people are running.  This should at least be indicated in a NEWS.Rd item for this fix (that there might be one-pixel changes in Cairo PNG output when drawing filled rectangles with no border).  For example, I think that Posit may have something like this for {ggplot2} (although it may not run on Cairo devices).  We should alert them to the possibility - they may even want to try the patch themselves to assess the impact.  George, do you happen to have a contact you could check with?
comments.creator: paul

comments.text:
Created attachment 3820
Updated patch

Kevin Ushey traced the bug to a [rounding problem in Cairo], but it's still worth working around it in R because the bug exists in so many versions of Cairo.

Updated the patch (the surrounding code now uses `bool` instead of `Rboolean`). `gdiff` tests reproduce the bug in `lattice::smoothScatter` and show it being fixed. There are other changes where rectangles now snap to a different row or column of pixels: 8 different examples in `lattice`; 20 different kinds of differences in `ggplot` (the total number of different files is 129 out of >2000).

[rounding problem in Cairo]: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/cairo/cairo/-/work_items/976
